findings.title: Isolated fix preview cannot use a supported custom MegaLinter configuration
findings.history_notes: new observation; no prior audit was available in this lane.
findings.observation: `Config::resolve` validates a `megalinter-config` and stores its normalized workspace-relative path (`src/config.rs:459–462`). `resolved_for_isolated_copy` subsequently requires that relative path to have the absolute original workspace as a prefix (`src/fix.rs:267–273`). Every supported nonempty custom selection therefore fails this conversion. Its subsequent candidate-absolute rewrite would also conflict with `ExecutionPlan`'s relative input contract.

evidence.description: In the probe, a clean repository containing committed `egolint.toml` and `.megalinter.yml` runs `fix` with an explicit linter selection. It exits 2 before any simulated runtime invocation, with the isolated-prefix configuration error and no preview patch. The otherwise equivalent default-configuration control exits 0, invokes the simulator once, and produces a patch. Both preserve the original source and clean index.

findings.why_it_matters: Repositories using the documented override/extension surface cannot use fix previews, even though planning and normal linting accept the same configuration. This is a functional failure, not an out-of-workspace write or exploit claim.
findings.recommendation: Preserve one documented relative-path representation through resolution and candidate planning. Resolve the selected committed config and its inheritance against the isolated candidate without reintroducing absolute paths or consulting live ignored inputs.
suggested_validation: End-to-end default and custom config previews, with a committed root-relative inherited policy, prove the selected config reaches the candidate runtime, expected patch is generated, original content/index stay unchanged, and escaping or unavailable candidate inputs still fail closed.
dependencies_or_risks: No identified work predecessor for a bounded repair. Retain the existing immutable-tree, runtime, and report boundaries. No real-image integration qualification was performed here.
findings.existing_issue_coverage: New focused fix-preview correctness issue, potentially shared with CORE-02 while retaining separate acceptance criteria. Existing issue #5 is the release program rather than a precise repair home.

findings.title: A committed executable file prevents isolated snapshot initialization
findings.area: Git snapshot construction for fix preview
findings.observation: `initialize_repository` creates a new Git repository, then calls `git update-index --chmod=+x` for executable paths before the initial `git add` (`src/fix.rs:810–823`). Those paths do not yet exist in the index.

evidence.description: A fresh committed synthetic consumer with one `100755` `script.sh` makes the actual `fix` command exit 3 with the empty-index/missing-`--add` Git error. No simulator is started and no patch is created. The original worktree remains clean and source unchanged. The non-executable default control succeeds.

findings.why_it_matters: Shell scripts, executable entrypoints, and other ordinary tracked executables make the preview feature unusable for otherwise supported repositories. This is not limited to a malformed or hostile tree.
findings.recommendation: Populate the trusted index before restoring executable modes (or explicitly use safe add semantics), retain the exact immutable base-tree equality check, and place a path separator before user-controlled paths in the index command.
suggested_validation: CLI preview on a clean consumer containing ordinary and executable files should reach the bounded runtime, preserve exact base mode/content identities, generate the intended patch, and leave the original untouched. Include a nested executable and a legal leading-dash filename; retain unsupported symlink/gitlink rejection. Platform claims require platform-specific evidence.
dependencies_or_risks: No identified predecessor for a bounded repair. Mode preservation is important on platforms whose filesystem does not express Git executable bits. Linux behavior was actually observed; no macOS/Windows result is claimed.
findings.existing_issue_coverage: The focused fix-preview correctness issue proposed for CORE-01, with this independent failure and acceptance retained.

findings.title: Focused canonical native reports can survive unrelated or failed later runs
findings.observation: The fixed `RUN_OWNED_ARTIFACTS` list removes raw MegaLinter reports, aggregate JSON/SARIF, debt, and patches, but omits `repository-continuity.json`, `repository-intelligence.json`, `repository-presentation.json`, `repository-release.json`, and `repository-gitignore.json` (`src/plan.rs:29–44`). `write_run_outputs` only rewrites optional focused reports when that capability is selected (`src/main.rs:1296–1341`); the focused gitignore command also writes a report outside that optional list.

evidence.description: The actual native CLI first runs an advisory intelligence policy successfully (exit 0) and writes an authentic focused intelligence report. A second `validate` without that selection exits 0 and writes a new aggregate that does not reference intelligence, while the old focused report remains byte-identical. A third attempt with a nonexistent policy fails, removes the aggregate during preparation, and still leaves the old focused report byte-identical. No real downstream publication or false consumer verdict is inferred from this local evidence.

findings.why_it_matters: A fixed report directory may contain canonical files from multiple runs or retain a previous focused verdict after a failed new invocation. Consumers or artifact uploads can mistake file presence for evidence of the latest invocation. This contradicts the documented stale-contract cleanup boundary even though individual files carry some source metadata.
findings.recommendation: Define the complete run-owned canonical artifact inventory and clear or explicitly invalidate each focused output at the appropriate lifecycle boundary. Alternatively use isolated run directories with an explicit manifest of the current run. Preserve unrelated private diagnostic retention deliberately.
suggested_validation: Generate real focused reports, then run without those capabilities and run with invalid inputs. Prove no stale focused artifact can represent the new run; verify current selected reports and aggregate references remain consistent and unrelated diagnostic files are retained according to policy. Cover command transitions including native-only, gitignore, and container-backed runs with a bounded simulator before qualifying real images.
dependencies_or_risks: No identified predecessor for a bounded repair. Coordinate all focused report owners and artifact consumers; avoid deleting arbitrary files under the reserved report directory or broadening its write authority.
findings.existing_issue_coverage: New focused native-report lifecycle/freshness repair. Existing #48 concerns checkpoint-audit report validation, a distinct content family.

findings.title: Presentation validation can accept missing checksum coverage and a missing banner descriptor
findings.observation: The manifest verifier only iterates entries that remain in files, and the banner/badge validation block runs only when a banner descriptor is present. It accepts an empty files object or a nonempty map that omits the referenced banner. It also accepts an Identity package with its banner descriptor deleted.

evidence.label: observed
evidence.detail: Missing file map is rejected, but an empty map is accepted and referenced asset coverage is not required.

evidence.label: observed
evidence.detail: Conditional destructuring skips all banner/badge checks when package.banner is missing.

evidence.label: observed
evidence.detail: presentation.control returns exit0/status valid/21 checked files. changed_banner_full_manifest returns exit1/status invalid with EGO-PRESENT-MANIFEST-001. Removing only the damaged banner's file entry yields exit0/status valid/20 checks; emptying the map yields exit0/status valid/0 checks. Deleting package.banner yields exit0/status valid/21 checks.

findings.why_it_matters: A publishable valid result can claim the Identity presentation is bound to checksums while the actual README banner has no verified checksum or the required descriptor is absent.
findings.recommendation: Validate required Identity package/manifest structure and cross-field coverage before declaring valid. Require a nonempty file map and checksum entries for every referenced banner/badge asset and descriptor that the pinned owner contract requires. Missing required descriptors must emit diagnostics rather than skip checks.
suggested_validation: Retain the passing complete-map control and damaged-file rejection.
Reject empty maps, nonempty maps omitting referenced assets, absent banner descriptors, and missing required descriptor-to-manifest bindings.
Keep advisory mode nonblocking while focused semantic status remains invalid; preserve offline behavior and authored files.
findings.dependencies_or_risks: No external predecessor identified for the bounded repair against current pinned contracts. Check exact Identity 3c2fd3 owner requirements and avoid inventing a new package contract or claiming pixel/accessibility certification.
findings.suggested_issue_home: New focused presentation-input/manifest-integrity bug. Do not reopen closed #27 or fold into future claim-engine #46.

findings.title: ADR and roadmap validators count fenced examples as live Markdown anatomy

Moving all ADR body anatomy into a markdown code fence, or putting the entire roadmap in a code fence, still produces valid source validation.

evidence.label: observed
evidence.detail: ADR anatomy uses starts_with and body.find without Markdown literal-region awareness.

evidence.label: observed
evidence.detail: Roadmap HTML comment extractor accepts any matching byte substring, including a literal example.

evidence.label: observed
evidence.detail: Roadmap evaluation scans these extracted comments and segment lines.

evidence.label: observed
evidence.detail: Control passes; removing Context returns invalid/1 diagnostic and empty roadmap invalid/2 diagnostics. Fencing the ADR body or entire roadmap returns exit0/status valid/0 diagnostics with 3 ADRs and 2 roadmap steps inspected.

findings.why_it_matters: A code sample can substitute for the actual required document structure or introduce phantom graph records, so semantic evidence can disagree with the rendered canonical document.
findings.recommendation: Use a bounded Markdown-aware representation or at least a shared literal-region scanner to exclude fenced/indented code and escaped examples from ADR anatomy, indexes, roadmap metadata, headings, and checklist counts. Keep source positions deterministic.
suggested_validation: Prove real required headings/metadata pass while fenced, indented, escaped, and inline literal examples do not satisfy required structure.
Include examples alongside real roadmap records so examples do not create duplicates or phantom graph edges.
Check heading level and exact required-section identity, source line locations, state/checklist matching, and existing historical fixtures.
findings.dependencies_or_risks: No external predecessor identified for the bounded current-contract repair. Preserve existing accepted ADR metadata/lifecycle and proposed roadmap authority; no graph policy promotion is implied.

findings.title: ADR link validation accepts empty GitHub identities and a hostless HTTP destination
findings.observation: The GitHub URL helper checks only that splitting owner/repo produces two components, without checking that either is nonempty. The general HTTP helper checks a prefix and a dot anywhere after ://, allowing a path dot to stand in for an authority.

evidence.label: observed
evidence.detail: HTTP and GitHub helpers use substring/count heuristics rather than host and repository components.

evidence.label: observed
evidence.detail: Replacing a fixture issue URL with https://github.com///issues/24 and adding external evidence URL https:///. still returns exit0/status valid/0 diagnostics under all eleven enabled blocking-profile rules.

findings.why_it_matters: Malformed reference strings can be recorded as structurally valid issue/evidence linkage. Offline validation cannot prove reachability or human approval, but it should not accept an absent authority or empty repository identity.
findings.recommendation: Parse the URI authority/path and require supported HTTP host and owner/repository/positive-number or full-commit components. Reuse strict repository and identifier validation; retain sanitized diagnostics and explicit separation from online reachability.
suggested_validation: Reject absent hosts, empty owner/repository segments, malformed commit references, credentials/control/whitespace ambiguities as appropriate to the pinned contract.
Retain valid supported HTTP(S), canonical GitHub issue/PR/commit, and historical evidence fixtures.
Do not fetch the destinations or treat structural success as publication/human approval.
findings.dependencies_or_risks: No external predecessor identified. This is a correctness finding about structure, not a demonstrated network exploit or authenticated-approval bypass.
findings.suggested_issue_home: New focused ADR/evidence URL-grammar bug; closed #24 delivered the baseline and does not cover this new repair.

findings.title: Release Task handoff validation treats echoed or commented commands as exact workflow dispatch
findings.observation: task_dispatches_workflow accepts any Task command string containing both gh workflow run and the declared workflow path. It cannot distinguish an echo from dispatch or bind the workflow path as the actual gh argument.

evidence.label: observed
evidence.detail: The boolean helper directly produces a passed Task handoff assertion.

evidence.label: observed
evidence.detail: The helper searches two substrings without command/argument binding.

evidence.label: observed
evidence.detail: Both echo gh workflow run .github/workflows/release.yml and gh workflow run .github/workflows/other.yml # .github/workflows/release.yml produce CLI0, focused state compliant, validation_complete true, 7/7 checks passed, including the exact-dispatch assertion. The normal dispatch control also passes.

findings.why_it_matters: A static conformance result asserts an exact publication handoff even when the declared command only prints text or dispatches a different workflow.
findings.recommendation: Define a small supported static dispatch form or structured handoff declaration, bind the actual command and workflow argument, and report unavailable when arbitrary shell cannot be proved. Do not execute Task commands to validate them or build an unrestricted shell interpreter.
suggested_validation: Reject or mark unavailable echo-only, comments-only, quoted documentation, different workflow arguments, and ambiguous compound shell forms.
Accept the documented direct dispatch and any explicitly supported structured equivalent; preserve exact source location and standard focused/run/SARIF agreement.
Extend #68's policy-boundary matrix with these cases, then include the repaired behavior in #69's dogfood.
findings.dependencies_or_risks: Current-v1 repair can start against existing accepted pins. Coordinate #29/#68/#69; do not wait for successor #76 or treat local conformance as remote publication evidence. Probe only validates source and never executes the synthetic Task commands.
findings.suggested_issue_home: Ledger lane recommends a focused current-v1 Task binding bug, coordinated with #68/#29; #68 remains the broader matrix, #69 the later dogfood.

findings.title: A contradictory not-applicable represented commit can still produce a valid Intelligence report
findings.area: Repository Intelligence / adoption and semantic status
findings.observation: The evaluator emits an adoption diagnostic when represented_commit is not-applicable while a source surface is present, but status aggregation ignores every adoption diagnostic for invalidity and only treats unknown/truncated evidence as incomplete.

evidence.label: observed
evidence.detail: Incomplete aggregation omits the present/not-applicable contradiction and invalid excludes ADOPTION_RULE.

evidence.label: observed
evidence.detail: validate_adoption explicitly diagnoses the incompatible selection.

evidence.label: observed
evidence.detail: With all eleven blocking-profile rules enabled and ADR, roadmap and commit-history present, --represented-commit not-applicable returns exit0/status valid, commits_inspected0, 3 ADRs, 2 roadmap steps, and an EGO-INTEL-ADOPTION-001 warning saying represented commit cannot be not-applicable while a source surface is present.

findings.why_it_matters: Machine consumers can see valid semantic status for a declared present source/history surface without its represented commit. The report itself identifies the contradiction but does not propagate it to the status.
findings.recommendation: Keep non-adoption, missing evidence, truncation, and contradictory adoption distinct. Make a present/not-applicable represented-source conflict invalid or explicitly incomplete under the supported contract; advisory enforcement must not upgrade that semantic state.
suggested_validation: Cover present surfaces with exact commit, unknown commit, not-applicable commit, all surfaces not-applicable, and truncated history.
Assert focused semantic status independently from process exit, rule severity and advisory/blocking enforcement.
Preserve the intentional scope of selected/disabled rules rather than silently enabling unrelated checks.
findings.dependencies_or_risks: No external predecessor identified for a bounded consistency repair. The caller still owns authentication of represented identity and source checkout; this finding does not claim that offline validation authenticates GitHub.
findings.suggested_issue_home: New focused Intelligence source/adoption-status consistency bug.

findings.title: Make native continuity validation agree with its exact pinned Aether schema
findings.observation: Five synthetic checkpoint variants disagree between native continuity semantic status and Draft202012Validator using the exact bundled Aether schema with registered format checks. Removing six required nullable keys, duplicating next.references, duplicating parallel_changes, or using an unpadded RFC3339 clock all remain native valid despite schema errors. A schema-valid lowercase t/z RFC3339 timestamp instead becomes native invalid. The control is accepted by both.

evidence.meaning: Option metadata fields decode missing keys as None, independently of schema required arrays.
The handwritten metadata validator checks selected fields but omits uniqueness on next references and parallel changes.
The handwritten datetime parser accepts variable-width clock fields and requires uppercase T/Z.
Exact normative structure used for the comparison.
Native focused semantic status, process result and actual pinned schema errors for control and five variants.

findings.why_it_matters: A consumer can receive valid structural evidence for a checkpoint that fails the selected portable contract, while another contract-valid checkpoint receives an invalid diagnosis. This is independent of observe-mode exit status, which intentionally remains nonblocking.
findings.recommendation: Treat the selected local schema as the authoritative structural contract, or prove equivalent typed validation for required nullable fields, uniqueness and RFC3339 semantics. Preserve offline source integrity and layered native freshness/privacy checks.
suggested_validation: A paired native/schema matrix covers every required nullable field independently, duplicate references and parallel changes, unsupported fields and formats.
Invalid unpadded timestamps produce structural findings; schema-valid lowercase RFC3339 delimiters preserve contract acceptance.
Observe changes effective severity without changing invalid semantic status; no upstream lifecycle promotion or source-pin relaxation is needed.
findings.dependencies_or_risks: No external predecessor identified for the bounded correction. Existing issue #55 owns broader continuity capability and released-input rollout acceptance; this parity repair must not claim ratchet/enforce promotion.
findings.proposed_issue_home: Focused startable defect linked to #55, or a clearly isolated #55 checkpoint; do not duplicate the whole upstream capability.

findings.title: Detect case-folded file/directory conflicts in native portability inventory
findings.observation: The native case checker indexes only complete leaf paths. A synthetic checkout containing the file Readme and directory README/page.md produces no EGO-PORT-CASE-001 finding and exits 0. The ordinary Readme.md/README.md control correctly produces the rule and exits 1. Differently cased ancestor directories with disjoint leaf names are also not represented by the current check.

evidence.meaning: case_collisions only folds each complete entry path.
Ordinary directory entries are not kept in the leaf inventory.
The selected rule promises ASCII case-insensitive path collision detection.
Positive full-path collision control and missed prefix topology cases.

findings.why_it_matters: On a case-insensitive filesystem, the same folded node cannot be both a file and a directory. Such a tree can pass native portability checks before a consumer encounters an unrepresentable checkout. No Windows or macOS checkout was executed during this audit; the native detection gap is directly observed, and the portability consequence follows from case-insensitive path identity.
findings.recommendation: Build a folded path-prefix topology from the inventory, including inferred ancestor directories, and report conflicting entry kinds and reviewed casing collisions deterministically. Preserve the intentional ASCII-only boundary.
suggested_validation: Keep the existing identical-leaf collision test.
Add case-folded file/directory prefix conflicts in both lexical orders and nested positions.
Cover disjoint leaf files beneath differently cased ancestors and ordinary case-consistent shared directories without false positives.
findings.dependencies_or_risks: No predecessor identified; pure native metadata semantics. Unicode and locale-specific filesystem equivalence remain outside the selected ASCII rule.
findings.proposed_issue_home: New focused native portability defect; no existing original issue specifically owns this gap.

findings.title: Recognize static multi-OS matrix.include rows in the workflow shell check
findings.observation: An equivalent two-OS workflow loses EGO-PORT-WORKFLOW-001 when matrix.os is expressed through static matrix.include rows rather than a direct array. Both fixtures select runs-on from matrix.os and omit shell. The direct-array control emits the advisory; the include form does not.

evidence.meaning: OS discovery only inspects direct sequence-of-string matrix axes and matches their key against runs-on; include rows are ignored.
The native pack advertises multi-OS workflow shell diagnostics.
Actual native command has no workflow-shell finding; the direct-array control has one.

findings.why_it_matters: A common static GitHub Actions matrix representation silently bypasses the selected advisory about differing default shell semantics. This remains a diagnostic-coverage issue, not proof that the fixture's echo command fails on either operating system.
findings.recommendation: Resolve statically declared include rows and scalar selector paths before deciding whether multiple OS families are possible. Keep dynamic or unsupported expressions explicitly bounded rather than guessing their values.
suggested_validation: Equivalent direct arrays and include rows produce the same advisory for an omitted shell.
Step, job and workflow default shells prevent the advisory in each supported static representation.
Single-OS, matrix.exclude refinements and unresolved dynamic selectors retain documented limits.
findings.dependencies_or_risks: No predecessor identified. The rule remains advisory and should not attempt general GitHub expression execution.
findings.proposed_issue_home: New small portability-diagnostic issue; may share an execution checkpoint with path-prefix coverage while retaining separate acceptance criteria.

findings.title: JavaScript package-quality normalization can turn failed or unsupported adapter evidence into a clean pass
findings.observation: The unchanged package-quality CLI returns 0 with OXLINT=passed and BIOME=passed when the explicitly stubbed Oxlint subprocess exits 1 but emits an empty diagnostics array. It also returns 0 and zero findings when both stubs emit the unsupported object envelope {}. runAdapter discards allowed process statuses and the normalizers substitute missing collections with empty arrays.
findings.why_it_matters: Malformed, incomplete or contradictory adapter evidence is labeled passed rather than unavailable/invalid/partial, weakening the stable quality-gate contract.
findings.recommendation: Preserve adapter status alongside payload, validate supported envelopes and reconcile nonzero exits with normalized findings. Emit an explicit non-clean result when evidence cannot explain a failure.
suggested_validation: Keep the clean pinned-adapter control.
Use trusted executable stubs for exit 1 with no diagnostics, empty/wrong-type envelopes and contradictory counts; require non-clean structured outcomes.
Retain real pinned Oxlint/Biome consumer fixtures to prove the supported adapter shapes.
Validate SARIF version and kind/level consistency. Pass records with level none or absent remain non-blocking; pass plus error is a malformed control, not a valid-pass regression.
dependencies_or_risks: No external predecessor identified for this repair.
Stubbed subprocess evidence proves orchestrator behavior only; it does not assert current pinned analyzers naturally emit these malformed shapes.
findings.existing_issue_coverage: No focused original issue. #35 covers the future general capability registry; #53 formatter ownership and #54 tool-gap evaluation do not cover this present adapter contract.

findings.title: JavaScript consumer manifest validation accepts fields forbidden by its published schema
findings.observation: The checked-in manifest schema has additionalProperties=false. A manifest with the unknown key profil_typo is schema-invalid but the unchanged CLI accepts it and returns 0 under clean stubbed adapters. validateManifest checks selected values without enforcing the closed object grammar.
findings.why_it_matters: Consumer typos and stale fields silently diverge from the public machine contract and can conceal configuration intent.
findings.recommendation: Validate manifests against the closed published contract or enforce the same grammar and unique-item constraints mechanically, preserving the one canonical schema.
suggested_validation: Unknown properties and duplicate ignore entries fail as configuration errors before adapters start.
Valid base and react-library manifests remain accepted.
Schema and runtime rejection agree for representative malformed values.

findings.title: JSONSkooma selector crashes on malformed mode types and accepts a boolean version
findings.observation: The actual Python launcher with mode=[] or mode={} raises an uncaught TypeError, exits 1 and emits no structured report. Its documented invalid-configuration path is exit 2 with JSON evidence. schema_version=true is accepted as version 1 and a disabled configuration exits 0.
findings.why_it_matters: Configuration failure is confused with validation findings and can leave consumers without an evidence artifact; boolean/integer coercion weakens the explicit version contract.
findings.recommendation: Validate types before set membership and version equality; route all supported malformed-configuration cases into the structured invalid_configuration outcome without launching Ruby.
suggested_validation: Wrong JSON types for mode/schema_version return exit 2 with structured invalid_configuration reports.
Boolean versions are rejected.
Valid disabled/auto/enabled activation and skip-before-Ruby behavior remain intact.
dependencies_or_risks: No Ruby installation is required to reproduce the observed selector failures.
findings.existing_issue_coverage: No focused original issue; #14 is already delivered/closed and #35's registry integration is distinct.

findings.title: JSONSkooma relative report location changes with the activation branch
findings.area: Optional Ruby schema adapter evidence routing
findings.observation: With --workspace selecting a different directory and the default relative report path, a skip writes the report beneath the invocation directory. The applicable branch invokes its child with cwd=workspace and passes the same relative report path, so a trusted Ruby stub writes beneath the selected workspace. The observed destination therefore depends on activation rather than one report-path rule.
findings.why_it_matters: Callers using the explicit workspace interface cannot reliably collect the same report location for skipped, unavailable and applicable runs.
findings.recommendation: Define one relative-report anchor and resolve it once before either local writing or child invocation, retaining stdout and explicitly supported absolute-output behavior.
suggested_validation: Invoke from a directory different from --workspace and check skip, invalid, unavailable, timed-out and applicable branches produce the same selected destination.
Keep --report '-' behavior and explicit absolute destinations covered.
Use a trusted child stub for routing tests and retain real Ruby fixtures for actual schema semantics.
dependencies_or_risks: The applicable routing control uses a stub, not actual Ruby validation.
findings.existing_issue_coverage: No focused original issue; separate from registry integration #35.

findings.title: Release input validation accepts non-object image and product records
findings.observation: The release-input validator treats a null image or product record as zero findings rather than invalid input. A copied actual CLI accepts a null full-engine product record with the correct environment; preserving all expected names while making every image/product record null also accepts an environment without any reviewed image values.
findings.why_it_matters: A named, present, but wrong-type source record can receive the same success message as a complete reviewed base-image/product contract. This weakens contract checks and can obscure accidental source corruption before the build.
findings.recommendation: Require every expected record to be an object, reject malformed nested element types without uncaught exceptions, and keep environment checking contingent on a structurally valid contract.
findings.suggested_validation: Replay positive reviewed data, every missing/non-object image and product record, wrong nested list/map element types, and missing/drifted environment values; assert a controlled nonzero diagnostic for invalid data and retain the existing valid-platform and environment controls.
findings.dependencies_or_risks: Independently startable from checked-in source; no release, registry, ARM64, or sibling capability predecessor is needed. This does not establish that a release can bypass later builds, artifact checks, protected environment, or promotion.

issue_coverage.recommended: focused new ready bug issue, coordinated with existing #5
issue_coverage.note: Existing #5 remains responsible for actual signed release and two pinned consumer adoptions; fixing this validator does not close #5.

findings.title: Missing requested native policy files use the internal-error exit category
findings.observation: `src/error.rs` defines missing requested paths as configuration exit 2, and `MissingPath` maps accordingly. The common native input reader maps missing ancestor/leaf metadata directly to `Filesystem` (`src/main.rs:1083–1087`), which maps to internal exit 4. Issue-title validation separately handles NotFound as `MissingPath`, so public commands disagree.

evidence.description: The third lifecycle probe runs `validate --repository-intelligence missing.toml --represented-commit unknown` in the same valid clean synthetic Git consumer and exits 4. The requested file does not exist; no decoder, runtime, or internal computation has failed.

findings.why_it_matters: Scripts distinguishing user input errors from internal failures get the wrong stable exit category. This does not alter the detected error or mean that a failed run passed.
findings.recommendation: Preserve NotFound as the documented missing-input/configuration category in the shared input reader, while retaining genuine permission/I/O/internal failures as their own categories.
suggested_validation: Public CLI missing native policy/suppression inputs return configuration exit 2; malformed input and genuine I/O failures retain distinct documented categories. Verify no stale current-run output survives these early failures (CORE-03).
dependencies_or_risks: No identified predecessor. Avoid recategorizing every filesystem error as configuration or weakening regular-file/path/budget checks.
findings.existing_issue_coverage: A small public CLI input/exit-contract repair, or a separate acceptance item in an explicitly bounded CLI contract consistency issue. Do not hide it inside the release program.

findings.title: Container guidance contradicts the reviewed full-engine platform boundary
findings.observation: The current container instructions request linux/amd64,linux/arm64 for egolint-full, call the reviewed MegaLinter base a manifest-list, and require both-architecture full-engine smokes.
